clue.text: Domestic help making tea

definitions.meaning: a charwoman or cleaner, shortened in British usage
British slang for a cup of tea, from the Hindi word

explanation.surface: A household servant brews a pot of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday British: a charlady is a cleaner, and a cuppa is slangily called by the same word.

clue.text: Rodent's place for resting by river

definitions.note: read as 'Rodent is', so the 's is a link to the wordplay

parts.note: a dormitory, shortened, is a room full of beds
the Ouse is a river in England (there are several of that name)

explanation.surface: A rodent's bed is beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Rodent' stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; 'by' just sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The small sleepy hibernating creature is a rodent, famous from Alice in Wonderland.

clue.text: Hairstyle, say, extremely uniform all over

indicators.note: over in a down clue turns the whole assembled string upside down, and all says it applies to everything before it

parts.note: to say is to tell

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, of the word uniform are used

explanation.surface: A haircut, for example, is uniformly the same everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a pointer to an example but is the verb TELL; 'all over' turns TELL + UM into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The short-front, long-back haircut is notorious; the word is also the name of a fish, fitting the puzzle's fishy entries.

clue.text: Criminals swipe cash with rope

indicators.note: a swipe is a wild swing, so the letters of the two words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Crooks steal money along with a length of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swipe' reads as 'steal' but signals an anagram of CASH and ROPE; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: People who illegally hunt game or fish on another's land are lawbreakers.

clue.text: Loud relative left before display

indicators.note: left is placed in front of the relative in the answer

parts.note: F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud
an aunt is a family relative

explanation.surface: A noisy family member left before the show.
explanation.definitionFit: To show off something ostentatiously is to put it on display.

clue.text: Go away singing jazz

definitions.meaning: an imperative telling someone to clear off, like shoo
improvised vocal jazz using nonsense syllables

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a brusque order to leave and the wordless improvised singing of jazz vocalists.

clue.text: Show it's worth revising at college

indicators.note: revising a text reworks it, so the letters of worth are rearranged

parts.note: being up means being in residence at a university

explanation.surface: Demonstrate that it pays to study at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link; UP for 'at college' is the British sense of going up to university.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something prominent or bring it to notice is a phrasal-verb synonym for show.

clue.text: Painter to cut back piece of hair

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read from right to left

parts.note: to lop is to cut off, as with branches
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: An artist is set to trim a strand of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' reads as the painter's intention, but those two words together are the verb being turned round by 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackson Pollock was the American abstract expressionist painter; the word is also a fish.

clue.text: Old racehorse not about to be beat

indicators.note: not indicates the letters for about are removed

parts.note: Red Rum was the famous British horse that won the Grand National three times in the 1970s
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A former racehorse is no longer about to be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum, a celebrated British steeplechaser, loses RE; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike repeatedly, as with sticks on a skin, is a verb synonym for beat.

clue.text: 1, 2, 3 … er … 5 … where's Dracula now?

parts.note: the numbers skip four, so the counter has forgotten where they were, and Dracula, being a nobleman of that title, has gone missing

explanation.surface: Someone counting stumbles, then asks where the vampire count has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: the counting fumbles a number, and the Transylvanian nobleman is mislaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgetting how far you have got in counting is the idiom; misplacing the vampire nobleman is the pun.

clue.text: Likewise, I'm a silly revolutionary to kidnap queen

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take the queen captive, holding her inside
revolutionary suggests turning things over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: In the same way, a foolish rebel plans to abduct the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges IMASILLY, and 'to kidnap' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs mean in the same manner, so one replaces the other in a sentence.

clue.text: Adult leaves award for university oink

indicators.note: the adult letter departs from the award word
for means in exchange, so the university letter takes the vacated place

parts.note: a grant is a sum awarded, for example to a student
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: An adult gives up a grant meant for university — and snorts.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise a pig makes is a snorting sound, a noun synonym for that farmyard sound.

clue.text: Good time to change sides with spirit

indicators.note: right swaps to left: the letter standing for right is replaced by the one for left

parts.note: an hour is a period of time

explanation.surface: A fine moment to defect and join a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change sides' swaps R (right) for L (left) in GHOUR; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A malevolent spirit that robs graves, a ghost-like monster of folklore.

clue.text: Wizards are most active on Sunday

indicators.note: active suggests lively movement, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Sorcerers are at their busiest on Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing S after the rearranged ARE MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard is informally a virtuoso, an expert or master performer.

clue.text: O for a really big limo!

definitions.note: the letter O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a limousine is a car

explanation.surface: An exclamation of wonder at a stretch limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O' looks like an exclamation but is the definition: the NATO phonetic code word for that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators spell the letter O with this code word in the NATO alphabet.

clue.text: Listen to music single

indicators.note: listen to signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: soul is a genre of music

explanation.surface: Hear the music single.
explanation.definitionFit: Only or lone is the adjectival meaning shared by single; it is also a flatfish.

clue.text: Transport around 50:50 animals

indicators.note: the vehicle goes around the two fifties

parts.note: a bus is a form of transport
L is the Roman numeral for 50, so two fifties give two of that letter

explanation.surface: Carrying animals with even odds of arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Male cattle are beasts, so the plural noun matches the plural animals.

clue.text: Are North Korea's leaders unstable, supporting plot to make things black?

indicators.note: in a down clue the jumbled letters sit beneath the plot, holding it up

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: unstable means the letters are not fixed and can be rearranged
leaders means the first letters of the words North and Korea

explanation.surface: Are the bosses in Pyongyang wobbly, backing a scheme to bring dark times?
explanation.walkthrough: 'unstable' rearranges ARE plus N and K into ARKEN; 'supporting' puts it below BED; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The literary verb means to darken, to make things gloomy or black.

clue.text: Boatman's a knave!

definitions.meaning: ... is an old informal word for a sailor, as in ... tar
the knave in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: The ferryman is a rogue!
explanation.walkthrough: 's a joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor is a jack tar, and the court card below the queen is called jack or knave; it is also a fish.

clue.text: No point to ripped Levi jeans, they can be chucked

indicators.note: ripped jeans are torn apart, so the letters are rearranged
no says the compass point is absent from the jeans letters

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Torn denim is pointless; it can be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No point' removes one E from LEVIJEANS; 'ripped' rearranges the rest; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spears thrown in athletics events are the things that get chucked.

clue.text: Struggle with fine? See below

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
lo is an archaic word for see or behold
under means below

explanation.surface: Battling with a penalty; see below for details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'See below' reads like a cross-reference but gives LO and UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To flail about helplessly is a verb synonym for struggle; it is also a flatfish.

clue.text: Not ready for difficult run? First, exercise!

indicators.note: difficult suggests tangled, so the letters of run are put in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, the first
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Unprepared for a hard run? Warm up first!
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' reads as an instruction to do something before but is I, one; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit not yet mature is not ready to eat.

clue.text: I have been taken in by Doctor Daley, perhaps

indicators.note: the contraction is enclosed by the doctor's letters

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: I have been fooled by a doctor named Daley, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Daley is a British Olympic diving medallist; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Daley is a famous example of someone who plunges from a high board.

clue.text: Ditches record into upturned shed

indicators.note: the record goes into the turned word
in a down clue, upturned turns the word shed upside down

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Throws a record into an overturned shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditches' looks like a verb but is the noun: LP goes into DEHS.
explanation.definitionFit: A delph is a regional word, chiefly in the Fens, for a drainage ditch.

clue.text: Left magnificent old pirate town

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
royal means splendid or magnificent

explanation.surface: Departed a splendid old buccaneer haven.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jamaican town was a notorious seventeenth-century buccaneer stronghold before an earthquake sank much of it.

clue.text: Pointy-headed staff in shop (IKEA)

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A spear on sale in a furniture store.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear with a pointed metal head; it is also a predatory freshwater fish.

clue.text: Heather Graham looks nice in fancy tops

indicators.note: fancy as a verb is to imagine, so the letters are reworked into a new order
tops means the first letters of the four words before it

explanation.surface: The actress Heather Graham looks good in stylish blouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather Graham' looks like the actress's name, but 'Heather' is the definition and 'Graham' starts the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the common heather plant; it is also a fish.

clue.text: Nothing turns head 90° for an emperor

indicators.note: the first letter, a Z, rotated a quarter turn looks like an N

parts.note: zero means nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing makes the head turn for an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: A Z on its side becomes an N; 'for an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman ruler said to have fiddled while Rome burned.

clue.text: Captain Kirk mostly gains power and potential energy on edge of space

indicators.note: on places the letter at the start of the rest
the edge means the first letter of the word space
the shortened name takes in the letters for power and energy
mostly drops the last letter of Kirk

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
PE is the abbreviation for potential energy

explanation.surface: Captain Kirk largely gains power and energy at the frontier of space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captain Kirk' looks like one name; 'Captain' is the definition. KIR takes in PPE to give KIPPER, a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The master of a ship or team leader is its captain.

clue.text: Black eyes see stars

definitions.meaning: slang for bruised eyes after a punch
things that shine brightly in the sky

explanation.surface: Someone with bruised eyes is seeing stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang names bruised eyes after their gleam, and anything that gleams like a star also shines; it is also a fish name.
